content:
NBC News reports that negotiations between Apple and OpenAI over alleged theft of trade secrets broke down because an outside lawyer for Apple mistakenly sent an email to another OpenAI employee, confusing the contacts between the two sides. Details below.

The report says Apple's outside legal counsel mixed up two email recipients

Last Friday, Apple filed a lawsuit accusing OpenAI Products and its two former employees, Chang Liu (張朗) and Tang Tan (陳唐), of stealing trade secrets.

In the lawsuit, Apple alleges its former employees stole confidential hardware information to advance OpenAI's positioning in the consumer device space.

Apple also accused OpenAI of failing to respond when the company first raised the matter directly in February:

However, according to NBC News, OpenAI said it did respond to Apple's initial outreach, but communications later broke down because an outside lawyer for Apple mistakenly sent an email to another OpenAI employee, confusing the recipient with someone else.

The report states that the outside lawyer representing Apple, Gabriel Gross (加布里埃爾·格羅斯) of the law firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges (加士德法律事務所), sent an email to OpenAI's general counsel Che Chang (張志), with the subject line "Former Apple employees retaining non-public, confidential, and proprietary information at OpenAI," and attached documents supporting Apple's allegations.

Thirteen minutes later, Gross sent another email to Chang, thanking him for taking a phone call during the period and for "providing cooperation so promptly."

The problem was that the second email was not sent to Chang, but to "an employee surnamed Wang (王) who had previously worked at Apple before moving to OpenAI," NBC News reported. Gross had earlier sent emails to both Chang and Wang, and had also spoken with Wang by phone, yet mistakenly replied to Chang.

Chang, believing Gross had sent him fabricated information to advance Apple's case against OpenAI, contacted two in-house lawyers at Apple, accusing the company's outside counsel of "falsely claiming to have spoken with me by phone," and added: "I don't know him, we have never spoken." He subsequently demanded that Gross be removed from the case.

Gross later apologized to Chang, and one of Apple's in-house lawyers told Chang that he could continue to liaise with Gross and his law firm as the case progressed. NBC News said: "It appears the negotiations between the two sides ended right there," adding that OpenAI claimed "no record of further outreach from Apple's lawyers was received until Apple formally filed on Friday."
